title: Snazzie FM News: The Pothole Files
description: Top of the hour on Snazzie FM News. Dale Crisp and Marsha Veld read the civic beat completely deadpan: the Elm Street sinkhole files for a parking permit, GreenFlow holds every light green for a third day, and the D M V reopens at the bottom of the hole. The anchors stay calm as the sinkhole quietly becomes a constituent.

lines.speaker: news-dale
lines.text: Top of the hour. Good evening, this is Snazzie FM News. I'm Dale Crisp.

lines.speaker: news-marsha
lines.text: And I'm Marsha Veld. Our developing top story, the Elm Street sinkhole.

lines.speaker: news-dale
lines.text: Public Works confirms the sinkhole has filed for a residential parking permit. It was approved ahead of nine human applicants.

lines.speaker: news-marsha
lines.text: A strong showing for a first-time resident. <p:0.3> In traffic, GreenFlow held every light green for a third straight day.

lines.speaker: news-dale
lines.text: The city calls that, quote, optimistic, and asks drivers to negotiate among themselves.

lines.speaker: news-marsha
lines.text: Returning to our developing story. The sinkhole has now applied for a seat on the zoning board.

lines.speaker: news-dale
lines.text: In related news, the D M V has reopened at the bottom of the sinkhole.

lines.speaker: news-marsha
lines.text: Officials note the wait time is now, technically, the same depth as the building.

lines.speaker: news-dale
lines.text: <p:0.3> And finally. The sinkhole could not be reached for comment, as it is now reachable only by descending into it.

lines.speaker: news-marsha
lines.text: Public Works asks that you do not. <p:0.3> That's the news.
